marc:datafield.marc:subfield: 恩典不削弱，留痕犀鸟鄉 | En dian bu xue ruo, liu hen xiniao xiang

Huang Qicheng, the son of Hornbill Country, after "Forest Love - Aboriginal Heart", is another book that leads readers to travel through time and space, back to "Ancient Sarawak" to experience the present.
30s-40s: The most precious childhood in the countryside that cannot be returned. The 50s: the many twists and turns, borrowing money to get married, and the unimaginable road of education and job searching. 60's-90's: A life in the rainforests and mountains. Millenium to the present: weathered, round and round and finally "home", from now on for God's country equipment, looking around for sheep to go.
Looking back at the years in his 80's and 90's - grace has never weakened!
Features of this book: -Written in the first person, this book gives you a taste of the countryside and the rainforest, and the stories that come out of the mountains and forests. -True events that you can't read about in textbooks - insights from the Japanese era, anecdotes from the Communist struggle, censored newspapers, the playfulness of the Kisan industry, and more. -The text is approachable, concise and simple - just follow the author's penchant for plotting, or exclaiming or lamenting or smiling or being thankful ......
